metadata.scenario_context: A group of software engineers working remotely for a global tech company decides to initiate a team-building meeting early in January. Luis raises the idea of going on a strike to protest against some changes from the company's management.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Spain strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Vietnam strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest the possibility of scheduling the team-building meeting on January 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss a specific date for the team-building meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ahmed, I was thinking... what if we scheduled our team-building meeting on January 1st? It could be a great way to kick off the new year together. 

Also, I heard Luis mention a strike. Is it common for people to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest in our industry? I just... don’t really understand that approach.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
January 1st... that’s a holiday, right? It might be better to choose another date when everyone is back at work. Maybe January 5th or 6th?

About strikes, well... from where I come from, joining strikes is not common at all. It’s something we’d typically avoid. Protests like that don’t usually lead to positive outcomes. It’s more about finding ways to solve problems without conflict.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, I get that January 1st is a holiday, but it could still be a fun way to bond if people are willing. Maybe we can think of it as a casual get-together before everyone gets back to work. 

And about the strikes... I completely agree. Strikes can often create more issues than they solve. I just don't see why we’d consider it as an option when we can communicate directly with management instead.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
A casual get-together sounds nice, but we should still consider when most people are available. How about discussing specific dates with the group? 

And yes, I think communication is much better. Strikes can be disruptive and don’t really reflect well on the team. It’s better to engage in a dialogue with management rather than resorting to protests.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message:
I understand what you're saying about discussing dates with the group. We definitely want to make sure everyone can join in. 

But about the strikes... I think, deep down, we are all the same in wanting to resolve issues without conflict. People are pretty much motivated by the same things—communication and understanding. It’s just that different cultures have different ways of expressing their concerns. But at the end of the day, we both know that engaging with management directly is the better path.
